takeaway: OmniFold unfolds T2K neutrino data by iteratively reweighting simulated detector events to match data (Step 1) and pulling those weights to reweight truth-level generator events (Step 2).
OmniFold reweights detector simulation to match data, transfers those weights to particle level, and feeds updated particle-level weights back into the simulation.

MINERvA double-differential neutrino event rates in muon longitudinal and transverse momenta are reasonably well described by MnvGENIE v1, illustrating the kinematic transition from quasi-elastic and resonant scattering at lower momentum to deep inelastic scattering at higher momentum.
MnvGENIE v1 broadly follows the data’s shapes but tends to undershoot higher-momentum bins, where the modeled DIS contribution becomes prominent.
The data generally lie above the predictions across much of the displayed phase space, and no model follows all the measured trends.

None of the generator models (untuned GENIE, NuWro, GiBUU) describe the measured MINERvA cross section relative to MnvGENIE v1 across the full 2D phase space, with agreement confined to low longitudinal momentum and intermediate transverse momentum.

Data/GiBUU exceeds unity in every displayed cell, sometimes substantially, while the other predictions show smaller, cell-dependent departures from unity.
